items.title: Independent classical Euclidean SU(2) Yang–Mills model
items.physical_scope: Adopted classical source-free Euclidean SU(2) model on closed oriented Riemannian four-manifolds, or R4 with a specified smooth S4 extension and finite action. No Lorentzian continuation, empirical assertion or quantum construction.
items.axiom_base: ZF + AC_omega through the specified gauge geometry; no integral Chern-class comparison is used.

items.statement:
Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, meaning that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function, for the specified smooth gauge-data and principal-connection constructions. Let $(X,g_X)$ be a connected, compact, oriented, finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold without boundary, with a supplied Riemannian metric. The alternative flat-space branch is standard oriented Euclidean $M=\mathbb R^4$ together with a fixed smooth trivialization outside a ball and a specified smooth extension $(\bar P,\bar A)$ over $X=S^4$ with its unit round metric, which is conformal to the flat metric in the stereographic chart; here $\bar A$ is a smooth principal connection one-form on $\bar P$. In the compact branch set $M=X$ and $(P,A)=(\bar P,\bar A)$. The extension and its transition map are part of the field data. Finite action alone is not asserted to imply such an extension. Write $g=g_X$ in the compact branch and $g=\delta$ in the flat branch.

Fix the global structure group $G=SU(2)=\{U\in M_2(\mathbb C):U^*U=I_2,\det U=1\}$, not its quotient, with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2)=\{X\in M_2(\mathbb C):X^*=-X,\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}X=0\}$ and commutator bracket. For $U\in SU(2)$ define $\operatorname{Ad}_U X:=UXU^{-1}$ for $X\in\mathfrak{su}(2)$. Let $\bar P\to X$ be a smooth right principal $SU(2)$-bundle: the right action is smooth, free, and transitive on each fibre, and local trivializations are equivariant. Its bundle-sector code $[\bar P]$, the nonempty minimum-rank set of codes of smoothly isomorphic bundles in the supplied non-Abelian gauge-data convention, belongs to the model-specified set $\Sigma$ of admitted bundle sectors. In the flat branch the physical bundle and connection are $P=\bar P|_M$ and $A=\bar A|_P$. An isomorphism here is a smooth equivariant diffeomorphism over $\operatorname{id}_X$, and $\Sigma$ may be a singleton. For the defining representation, use the Pauli matrices $\sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}$, and $\sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$, and put $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$. The earlier lemma *Compactness and normalized invariant form for SU(2)* states that $T_1,T_2,T_3$ form a real basis of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and that $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(XY)$ is a positive-definite symmetric real bilinear form with $\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$ and $\kappa(\operatorname{Ad}_U X,\operatorname{Ad}_U Y)=\kappa(X,Y)$ for all $U\in SU(2)$ and $X,Y\in\mathfrak{su}(2)$. Writing $\bar\omega:=\bar A$, this principal connection one-form satisfies $R_g^*\bar\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\bar\omega$ and $\bar\omega(\xi_{\bar P})=\xi$ for each $g\in SU(2)$ and $\xi\in\mathfrak{su}(2)$, where $R_g(p)=pg$ and $\xi_{\bar P}(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_0p\exp_{SU(2)}(t\xi)$. In a local section $s_i$ of $\bar P$, write $A_i=s_i^*\bar\omega$ and $F_i=dA_i+\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$; the alternating wedge–Lie bracket is normalized by $\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i](Y,Z)=[A_i(Y),A_i(Z)]$. The Hodge star is determined by $\alpha\wedge *_{g_X}\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_{g_X}\,d\operatorname{vol}_{g_X}$ on two-forms, acts on the form part of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued forms, and satisfies $*_{g_X}^2=1$ there.

The principal-curvature result gives $F_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{u_{ij}^{-1}}F_i$ on an overlap where $s_j=s_i u_{ij}$. Hence the $F_i$ are local representatives of one global curvature $F_{\bar A}$; in the compact branch put $F_A=F_{\bar A}$ and in the flat branch put $F_A=F_{\bar A}|_M$. For smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued $p$- and $q$-forms $\alpha=\sum_{a=1}^3T_a\alpha^a$ and $\beta=\sum_{b=1}^3T_b\beta^b$, with real-valued coefficient forms $\alpha^a$ and $\beta^b$, define their coefficientwise pairing by

$$\kappa(\alpha\wedge\beta):=\sum_{a,b=1}^3\kappa(T_a,T_b)\,\alpha^a\wedge\beta^b.$$

This is independent of the chosen basis. The $\operatorname{Ad}$-invariance of $\kappa$ and the stated curvature transition law make the local four-forms $\kappa(F_i\wedge *_g F_i)$ agree on overlaps; they therefore define a global four-form, denoted $\kappa(F_A\wedge *_gF_A)$ in the action. Adopt, independently of any Lorentzian theory, the source-free pure Euclidean $SU(2)$ model on exactly these supplied geometric data. No matter fields are present. Fix a dimensionless coupling $g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$. In natural units $c=\hbar=1$, $A_\mu$ has mass dimension one and $F_{\mu\nu}$ mass dimension two. Adopt the dimensionless action

$$S_E[A]=\frac{1}{2g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}\int_M\kappa(F_A\wedge *_gF_A).$$

In the flat-space branch require finite action in addition to the specified smooth compactification extension. Smooth gauge transformations are equivariant bundle automorphisms covering the identity; the action is evaluated on the supplied admissible connection. Classical stationarity means vanishing first variation for smooth compactly supported adjoint-bundle-valued one-form variations preserving the supplied extension/boundary data. On a closed base every smooth variation has compact support.

This is a classical Euclidean model assumption. It neither derives a Euclidean theory by Wick rotation from a Lorentzian postulate nor asserts empirical confirmation, reflection positivity, a functional measure, gauge fixing, a convergent quantum integral, or a continuum quantum theory. The closed-manifold formulation is the explicitly adopted geometric extension of the cited flat Euclidean action; finite action alone is not claimed to prove removable singularities or compactification.

items.title: Euclidean Yang–Mills sectors and instanton interpretation
items.design_state: Owner repaired: independent Euclidean postulate supplies the model assumption.
items.statement:
Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, meaning that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function, for the specified smooth gauge-data and principal-connection constructions. Let $(X,g_X)$ be a connected, compact, oriented, finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold without boundary, with a supplied Riemannian metric. The alternative flat-space branch is standard oriented Euclidean $M=\mathbb R^4$ together with a fixed smooth trivialization outside a ball and a specified smooth extension $(\bar P,\bar A)$ over $X=S^4$ with its unit round metric, which is conformal to the flat metric in the stereographic chart; here $\bar A$ is a smooth principal connection one-form on $\bar P$. In the compact branch set $M=X$ and $(P,A)=(\bar P,\bar A)$. In the flat branch set $P=\bar P|_M$ and $A=\bar A|_P$. The extension and its transition map are part of the field data. Finite action alone is not asserted to imply such an extension. Write $g=g_X$ in the compact branch and $g=\delta$ in the flat branch.

Fix the global structure group $G=SU(2)$, not its quotient, and let $\bar P\to X$ be a smooth right principal $SU(2)$-bundle: the right action is smooth, free, and transitive on each fibre, and local trivializations are equivariant. Its bundle-sector code $[\bar P]$, the nonempty minimum-rank set of codes of smoothly isomorphic bundles in the supplied non-Abelian gauge-data convention, belongs to the model-specified set $\Sigma$ of admitted bundle sectors. An isomorphism here is a smooth equivariant diffeomorphism over $\operatorname{id}_X$, and $\Sigma$ may be a singleton. Writing $\bar\omega:=\bar A$, this smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued principal connection one-form satisfies $R_g^*\bar\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\bar\omega$ and $\bar\omega(\xi_{\bar P})=\xi$, where $\xi_{\bar P}(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_0p\exp_{SU(2)}(t\xi)$. In a local section $s_i$ of $\bar P$, write $A_i=s_i^*\bar\omega$ and $F_i=dA_i+\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$; the alternating wedge–Lie bracket is normalized by $\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i](Y,Z)=[A_i(Y),A_i(Z)]$. The Hodge star is determined by $\alpha\wedge *_{g_X}\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_{g_X}\,d\operatorname{vol}_{g_X}$ on two-forms, acts on the form part of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued forms, and satisfies $*_{g_X}^2=1$ there. The earlier lemma *Principal curvature, Cartan structure equation, and Bianchi identity* shows that the $F_i$ are local representatives of the global curvature $F_{\bar A}$; $F_A$ denotes its restriction to $M$, and in the compact branch $F_A=F_{\bar A}$.

Work under the independent physical assumption in the earlier postulate *Independent classical Euclidean SU(2) Yang–Mills model*, on precisely the geometric data specified above: it is source-free pure $SU(2)$, contains no matter fields, and adopts the action below independently of the Lorentzian model; no Wick-rotation inference is made. Use anti-Hermitian defining-representation generators with $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(T_aT_b)=-\tfrac12\delta_{ab}$, the positive invariant form $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(XY)$, and a fixed dimensionless coupling $g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$. In natural units $c=\hbar=1$, $A_\mu$ has mass dimension one, $F_{\mu\nu}$ has mass dimension two, and $S_E/\hbar$ is dimensionless. The conditional Euclidean action is

$$S_E[A]=\frac{1}{2g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}\int_M\kappa(F_A\wedge *_gF_A).$$

In the flat-space branch admissibility also requires $S_E[A]<\infty$ on $\mathbb R^4$. For $U,V\in\mathfrak{su}(2)$ define $B_{\mathrm{top}}(U,V):=-\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(UV)=\kappa(U,V)/2$. The mathematical charge used here is the supplied trace-normalized charge of the compactified connection,

$$\nu(\bar P,\bar A)=\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_X B_{\mathrm{top}}(F_{\bar A}\wedge F_{\bar A})=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_X\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(F_{\bar A}\wedge F_{\bar A})=-\langle c_2(\bar E_{\mathbf2}),[X]\rangle\in\mathbb Z,$$

where $\bar E_{\mathbf2}=\bar P\times_{\mathbf2}\mathbb C^2$ and the final equality uses the supplied instanton-number definition with its full-Axiom-of-Choice and Chern–Weil hypotheses. This sign makes a positive-charge self-dual configuration satisfy $F_{\bar A}=*_{g_X}F_{\bar A}$ and a negative-charge anti-self-dual configuration satisfy $F_{\bar A}=-*_{g_X}F_{\bar A}$ on the compactified base. The charge label is not asserted to classify every connected component or every gauge orbit.

For each sector code $s\in\Sigma$, the model supplies one representative smooth right principal bundle $\bar P_s\to X$ with $[\bar P_s]=s$, taking $\bar P_{[\bar P]}=\bar P$ for the selected bundle. In the flat-space branch use its restriction $P_s=\bar P_s|_M$ and its specified smooth compactification extension. Let $\mathcal A_\nu(\Sigma)$ denote the set of tagged pairs $(s,A)$, where $s\in\Sigma$ and $A$ is an admissible smooth connection on that supplied representative whose compactified charge is $\nu$. Each connection space is a set of smooth one-forms on the specified total space, and the supplied set-indexed family makes this tagged union a set. The representatives are part of the model data; changing them transports connection data by bundle isomorphisms, and no universal choice of representatives is asserted. In the flat-space branch, admissible connections are required to have the specified smooth extension and finite Euclidean action.

A classical Euclidean saddle is a smooth admissible connection whose first variation of $S_E$ vanishes for every smooth compactly supported connection variation preserving the boundary data. An instanton (respectively anti-instanton) saddle is a nonzero-charge saddle satisfying the positive (respectively negative) self-duality equation. Let $\mathcal A(\Sigma):=\bigsqcup_{\nu\in\mathbb Z}\mathcal A_\nu(\Sigma)$ be the tagged disjoint union of the admissible connection spaces over the model-specified bundle sectors. A source observable is a complex-valued function $O:\mathcal A(\Sigma)\to\mathbb C$ that is constant on connection data related by a smooth diffeomorphism $\Phi:P\to P$ satisfying $\pi\circ\Phi=\pi$ and $\Phi(pg)=\Phi(p)g$ for all $p\in P$ and $g\in SU(2)$. No continuity, measurability, or other regularity of $O$ is assumed. Gauge transformations are these smooth principal-bundle automorphisms.

The notation

$$Z_{\mathrm{formal}}(\theta;O)=\sum_{\nu}e^{i\theta\nu}\int_{\mathcal A_{\nu}(\Sigma)}\mathcal D A\;O[A]e^{-S_E[A]}$$

denotes only a formal continuum sector expression over connections, with gauge redundancy left untreated. Here $\theta$ is dimensionless and has period $2\pi$ when $\nu$ is integral. No continuity, measurability, or other regularity of the formal expression is asserted. The notation defines no functional measure, gauge fixing or orbit-volume prescription, determinant, convergent integral, Hilbert-space sector, or continuum quantum field theory, and selects no finite regulator or limit.

items.title: The trivial Euclidean vacuum lies in the zero-charge sector
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; readiness escalated with the assigned page Euclidean model prerequisite unresolved.
items.statement: Assume full AC, meaning that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; in particular, countable choice holds. Let $M=S^4$ be a connected compact oriented smooth four-manifold with a chosen orientation and any smooth Riemannian metric, let $SU(2)=\{U\in M_2(\mathbb C):U^*U=I_2,\det U=1\}$, and set $P=M\times SU(2)$ with projection $\pi(x,U)=x$ and right action $(x,U)\cdot V=(x,UV)$. In its global product trivialization take the zero connection potential $A=0$, with curvature $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$. In the independent Euclidean $SU(2)$ model, fix $g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$ and $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(XY)$ with its coefficientwise extension to Lie-algebra-valued forms; the action is $S_E[A]=(2g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2)^{-1}\int_M\kappa(F_A\wedge *_gF_A)$. The compactified charge is $\nu(P,A)=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_M\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(F_A\wedge F_A)$. A classical saddle is a smooth admissible connection whose first variation of $S_E$ vanishes for every smooth compactly supported connection variation preserving the supplied boundary data. With these action, charge, and saddle definitions, this configuration has $F_A=0$, $\nu(P,A)=0$, and $S_E[A]=0$. It is a classical saddle in the trivial sector, and it is not a nonzero-charge instanton saddle.

Assume full AC, meaning that every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; in particular, countable choice holds. Let $S^4=\{z\in\mathbb R^5:|z|=1\}$ have its unit round metric. Put $p_\infty=(0,0,0,0,-1)$ and $p_0=(0,0,0,0,1)$. Specify the inverse stereographic maps $\kappa_N:\mathbb R^4	o U_N:=S^4\setminus\{p_\infty\}$ and $\kappa_S:\mathbb R^4	o U_S:=S^4\setminus\{p_0\}$ by $\kappa_N(x)=(2x/(1+|x|^2),(1-|x|^2)/(1+|x|^2))$ and $\kappa_S(y)=(2y/(1+|y|^2),(|y|^2-1)/(1+|y|^2))$. Here $x$ and $y$ denote their inverse coordinates on $U_N$ and $U_S$, respectively; orient $S^4$ so $dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\wedge dx^4>0$. In the north chart put $r^2=\sum_{\mu=1}^4(x^\mu)^2$; the metric is $4(1+r^2)^{-2}\sum_\mu(dx^\mu)^2$. In the south chart put $y=x/r^2$; the metric is $4(1+|y|^2)^{-2}\sum_\mu(dy^\mu)^2$. Define $SU(2)=\{U\in M_2(\mathbb C):U^*U=I_2,\det U=1\}$, with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2)=\{X\in M_2(\mathbb C):X^*=-X,\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}X=0\}$ and commutator bracket; for $U\in SU(2)$ set $\operatorname{Ad}_U X:=UXU^{-1}$. Use the Pauli matrices $\sigma_1= egin{pmatrix}0&1\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_2= egin{pmatrix}0&-i\i&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_3= egin{pmatrix}1&0\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$ and anti-Hermitian generators $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$ with $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(T_aT_b)=-	frac12\delta_{ab}$. Let $\epsilon_{ijk}$ be totally antisymmetric with $\epsilon_{123}=1$, set $\eta_{aij}=\epsilon_{aij}$, $\eta_{ai4}=\delta_{ai}$, $ ar\eta_{aij}=-\epsilon_{aij}$, and $ ar\eta_{ai4}=\delta_{ai}$ for $i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$, and extend both arrays antisymmetrically in their last two indices. For any $ho>0$, put $u(x)=(x^4I_2-i x^j\sigma_j)/r$ on the overlap, and glue two trivial right $SU(2)$ bundles with local sections satisfying $s_S=s_Nu^{-1}$. The local connection potentials are

$$A_N= rac{2\eta_{a\mu
u}x^

u}{1+ho^2|y|^2}T_a\,dy^\mu.$$

On the overlap the potentials obey $A_S=\operatorname{Ad}_uA_N+u\,d(u^{-1})$, with the right-action section convention above. Their curvature representatives are $F_N=dA_N+	frac12[A_N\wedge A_N]$ and $F_S=dA_S+	frac12[A_S\wedge A_S]$, using the alternating wedge–Lie bracket normalized by $	frac12[A\wedge A](Y,Z)=[A(Y),A(Z)]$; the transition makes them representatives of one global adjoint-bundle-valued curvature $F$. For smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued forms $\alpha=\sum_aT_a\alpha^a$ and $ eta=\sum_bT_b eta^b$ with real coefficient forms, use $\kappa(\alpha\wedge eta)=\sum_{a,b}\kappa(T_a,T_b)\alpha^a\wedge eta^b$, where $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(XY)$. The conditional Euclidean action is $S_E=(2g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}\kappa(F\wedge *F)$, and the compactified charge $
u=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(F\wedge F)$, for fixed $g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$. For this specified smooth two-chart connection, the charge is $
u=1$, the curvature is self-dual, and $S_E=8\pi^2/g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2$. A classical saddle means a smooth admissible connection whose first variation of $S_E$ vanishes for every smooth compactly supported adjoint-bundle-valued one-form variation preserving the supplied data. This connection is a classical saddle, and its nonzero charge and self-duality make it an instanton saddle. If the formal sector expression includes the dimensionless theta coupling $	heta$, the corresponding formal single-saddle factor is $e^{-8\pi^2/g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2+i	heta}$. This factor is not an evaluated continuum path integral.
